glosses: to select, to pick (to choose one or more elements from a set)
selecteren; uitkiezen
wybierać, selekcjonować
Choisir (généralement le meilleur ou les meilleurs) parmi un groupe.

examples.text: Roger, le patron, apportait naturellement un soin maniaque à sélectionner les produits qu'il proposait à sa clientèle, qu'il s'agisse de charcutaille, de fromage ou de pichtegorne.

glosses: Privileged, specially selected.

examples.text: Only a select few were allowed into the premiere.
A few select spirits had separated from the crowd, and formed a fit audience round a far greater teacher.

At half-past nine on this Saturday evening, the parlour of the Salutation Inn, High Holborn, contained most of its customary visitors.[…]In former days every tavern of repute kept such a room for its own select circle, a club, or society, of habitués, who met every evening, for a pipe and a cheerful glass.

glosses: Of high quality; top-notch.

examples.text: This is a select cut of beef.
The two sisters at once called on Mrs. Bolton, in a newish house in a row, quite select for Tevershall.

glosses: To choose one or more elements of a set, especially a set of options.

examples.text: He looked over the menu, and selected the roast beef.
The program computes all the students' grades, then selects a random sample for human verification.

glosses: To obtain a set of data from a database using a query.
To retrieve from personal or computer memory.

examples.text: I remember looking in the card catalogue of the main Public Library under "Homosexuality" and not daring to call up the books because "they" might think I was one.
The Emoji Movie takes place in “Textopolis,” where emojis maintain their assigned expression with no deviation, waiting to be called up for their on-screen appearance as needed.

glosses: To summon (someone) to report for military service.

examples.text: “I don’t know if I’ll go to war or not, I don’t know what process the guys who are being called up are going through,” he wrote. “At the moment, our army is fully coping with the offensives of Russian soldiers and equipment.”

glosses: To select e.g. to a sports squad.

examples.text: Dean Ashton was called up to the England squad for the first time.

glosses: To call on the telephone.

examples.text: You take that book Of Human Bondage, by Somerset Maugham, though. I read it last summer. It’s a pretty good book and all, but I wouldn’t want to call Somerset Maugham up. I don’t know. He just isn't the kind of a guy I'd want to call up, that's all.

The other night, you wouldn't believe
The dream I just had about you and me
I called you up, but we both agree

glosses: Elegir, escoger, especialmente mediante una selección o votación.

examples.text: «La programación infantil tiene asignado un horario y es mejor que los niños se limiten a él. Los padres deben seleccionar los programas que quieren que sus hijos vean (si es posible, lo ideal sería haberlos visionado previamente para saber a qué atenerse) y, siempre que se pueda, verlos junto a ellos».
